@sc1-moo 

This is actually expected behavior, not a browser bug.

The content inside `<textarea>` is treated as literal text, including tabs, spaces, and line breaks used for indentation. So when the element is written like this:
```html
<textarea>
	Some text
</textarea>
```
the tab and newline become part of the textarea value itself.

That is different from most HTML elements where indentation is ignored visually. `<textarea>` intentionally preserves whitespace exactly as written, similar to `<pre>`.

If you want an empty textarea, it must be written without inner whitespace:
```html
<textarea></textarea>
```
or use the `placeholder` attribute instead.

So the behavior is consistent with the HTML specification and likely not considered an issue in the standard itself.

Hello Grenish,

Beware to not mistake two things:
- I am not talking about then content *in between* the 2 tag textarea.

I am actually talking about tabs on the *← ← ←left* of the tag 
<textarea>, tabs used for indentation.

so :
<html>
     <body>
         <textarea>
             placeholder="suggestion..."
         </textarea>
     </body>
</html>
will produce a textarea box with 2x %09 inside and preclude to see the 
"suggestion..."

Whilst
<html>
     <body>
<textarea>
placeholder="suggestion..."
</textarea>
     </body>
</html>
will produce a textarea box with no %09 inside and let see the 
"suggestion".

No offence, but I am quite sure the HTML specification define what 
happen inside in between the tags and not before, on their left side ...

I do not know if that was my explanation to mislead you.
I hope I have manage to clarify it.
:)

Hello @sc1-moo,

I think I understand your point now.

You are not referring to indentation before the `<textarea>` tag itself, but to the indentation that becomes part of the text node inside the textarea after the opening tag.

So these two examples are parsed differently:
```html
<textarea>
             placeholder="suggestion..."
</textarea>
```
produces a textarea value similar to:

```
             placeholder="suggestion..."
```

while:
```html
<textarea>
placeholder="suggestion..."
</textarea>
```
produces:

```
placeholder="suggestion..."
```

Because `<textarea>` treats its child text as raw text content, the indentation whitespace is preserved and rendered inside the control. That is why the first example visually starts with a large left offset while the second one does not.

This behavior is expected according to the HTML specification and is not considered a browser bug.

Relevant references:

> "The raw value is the value as it was originally set. It is not normalized." [HTML Standard: The textarea element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-textarea-element)

- [MDN: `<textarea>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/textarea)

In particular, `<textarea>` preserves literal text content and whitespace similarly to `<pre>`, unlike most HTML elements where indentation is visually ignored.

So the observed `%09` characters are simply preserved tab characters from the textarea's inner text content.

Hope this helps.
